issues.title: Invalid scalar interpolation in the homotopy proof
issues.failure_explanation: If [a]=[a+n] in R/Z, then [t(a+n)]=[ta+tn], which generally differs from [ta] for t in (0,1). Hence the displayed F depends on representatives and does not define the continuous map required by def.homotopy. Equality of winding vectors only shows that f/g has zero winding; a global real lift of that quotient is still needed.
issues.overall_effect: The converse implication in thm.homotopy is unproved, so the claimed classification of homotopy classes by the winding vector is unsupported by the old argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the converse proof by setting h=f/g, proving that its zero winding on every triangular basis loop yields a continuous real lift h(x)=exp(2πiφ(x)) on all of G, and then using F(t,x)=g(x)exp(2πi(1-t)φ(x)) as a homotopy from f to g. The lift can be constructed compatibly on the dense union of triangular boundaries and extended after establishing uniform continuity.
issues.why_classification: The theorem survives unchanged, but passing from zero winding data to a global lift on the Sierpinski gasket requires a contained, nontrivial lifting argument and supporting lemmas. This is more than a routine local correction, while it neither requires paper-wide reconstruction nor causes mathematical loss.

issues.title: Missing square in the circle-valued Dirichlet energy
issues.failure_explanation: On a sufficiently short edge, a local real lift has increment a and the geodesic distance is |a| under the paper's quotient normalization. EGamma contributes a squared term, whereas the old Em-hat contributes only |a|. Thus the asserted equality with the lifted quadratic energy and the resulting minimizer interpretation cannot follow from the displayed old definition.
issues.overall_effect: The old circle functional is not the quadratic Dirichlet energy used by the lifting and minimization argument, invalidating the stated variational identification. This does not by itself contradict the separately constructed harmonic lift.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing square and define the functional by hat E_m(f)=(5/3)^m sum_{x∼_m y} d_T(f(x),f(y))^2. With this definition, sufficiently short-edge real lifts identify the circle energy with the quadratic lifted energy used in the minimization argument.
issues.why_classification: The square is uniquely forced by the surrounding quadratic Dirichlet form, the definition of E[Γ_m^0], and the asserted equality between the two energies. Correcting the omitted exponent repairs no inference or construction and withdraws no coherent guarantee.

issues.title: Missing winding compatibility in the p.c.f. cycle embedding

failure_location.quote: Restricting to the fundamental domain and projecting the range to $\mathbb{T}$ yields the desired harmonic map.

issues.failure_explanation: The old proof glues sheets with shift rho_i at a cut on the successor cycle iota(gamma_i). This establishes the intended monodromy on that successor cycle, but eq:winding_vec_general prescribes winding on gamma_i itself. Vertex containment and the pairwise-intersection condition do not establish that the two loops are homologous or have equal winding, so the final projection has not been shown to satisfy the theorem's prescribed degree vector.
issues.overall_effect: The existence assertion in thm.pcf is not established under the old embedding assumptions for the stated basis-cycle winding data.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the cycle-embedding hypotheses in thm.pcf by requiring each successor cycle iota(γ_i^(m)) to represent the same homology class as γ_i^(m), equivalently to define the same winding functional on circle-valued maps. Under this explicit hypothesis, the jump ρ_i imposed at the cut on iota(γ_i^(m)) gives the prescribed winding on γ_i^(m), so the existing covering-space and minimization construction applies.
issues.why_classification: This is a local repair of the theorem's assumptions and leaves the construction and existence conclusion intact, but it adds a genuinely stronger topological compatibility condition rather than merely excluding an exceptional degeneracy. The resulting theorem is recognizably comparable and the weakening is limited, so the issue is moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Undefined boundary-cycle winding in the p.c.f. theorem

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\gamma_0\in\operatorname{Cyc}(\Gamma_m)$ be a cycle that contains boundary vertices $V_0\subset V(\gamma_0)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem invokes pcf-bc-hm, but its parameter rho_0 is identified with the winding on an undefined object p. The only cycle introduced for traversing all boundary vertices is gamma_0, and the prescribed basis windings determine its winding. As written, however, the boundary-value input used by thm.pcf is not defined.
issues.overall_effect: The boundary condition invoked in thm.pcf is literally ill-defined, although the intended boundary cycle is unambiguous from the adjacent setup.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the undefined p by the previously introduced boundary cycle γ_0 and define ρ_0=ω_{γ_0}(f). If γ_0=sum_i a_iγ_i^(m) in the chosen cycle basis, state equivalently that ρ_0=sum_i a_iρ_i.
issues.why_classification: The adjacent setup uniquely identifies γ_0 as the intended boundary cycle, and its winding is already determined by the prescribed basis windings. The correction is purely notational and requires no change to the theorem or its argument.
